diagnosis.incident_summary: Order flow has been degraded since 11:16 UTC when a malformed line in partner batch PB-4471 poisoned the order.enriched offset, crash-looping order-orchestrator on a fixed 3-minute interval with the consumer never advancing past offset 4,481,209.

timeline.description: Partner B2B batch PB-4471 accepted: 380 lines, 1 malformed (negative line quantity, SKU MRD-88213 qty=-4)
Deserialisation exception consuming order.enriched offset 4481209: negative quantity not allowed for field 'lineQty' (value=-4)
pod ord-orch-svc-b91c restart 1: consumer re-attempted offset 4481209 after deserialisation failure
consumer offset on order.enriched frozen at 4,481,209 — has not advanced since the poisoned message was first attempted
pod ord-orch-svc-b91c restart 2: consumer re-attempted offset 4481209 after deserialisation failure
pod ord-orch-svc-b91c restart 3: consumer re-attempted offset 4481209 after deserialisation failure
pod ord-orch-svc-b91c restart 4: consumer re-attempted offset 4481209 after deserialisation failure

hypotheses.cause: Poison message on order.enriched: order-orchestrator's consumer is stuck retrying a single malformed offset

supports.why: Deserialisation exception names the exact offset (4481209) and the exact malformed field (negative lineQty=-4) — a deterministic, reproducible failure, not a resource condition.
Every restart re-attempts the same offset 4481209 — the consumer is not making progress, it is retrying.
Restarts land at 11:19:05, exactly 3 minutes after the previous one — a metronomic interval is a restart-policy artefact, not organic load-driven crashing.
Third restart, same offset, same 3-minute spacing — confirms the pattern is not decaying or changing shape.
The committed offset on order.enriched has not moved since 11:16 despite four restarts — direct, checkable proof the consumer is blocked on one record.

contradicts.why: The order.enriched.DLQ topic sits at depth zero throughout, which on its face could be read as 'nothing was ever rejected, so maybe this isn't a poisoned record' — though the more complete read is that no DLQ policy is configured on this topic at all, so a zero DLQ depth is not informative either way.

hypotheses.what_would_change_this: If the consumer offset were advancing (even slowly) between restarts, or if restarts had irregular timing, that would point away from a single stuck record and back toward a resource or load-driven cause.

hypotheses.cause: Memory pressure on order-orchestrator causing OOM restarts

supports.why: Repeated pod restarts are superficially consistent with an OOM crash loop, which is the pattern seen in a comparable incident (S1) on a different service.

contradicts.why: Heap (46.6%) and CPU (27.5%) on order-orchestrator are both within normal baseline range at the same timestamp as an active restart — resource exhaustion is not present.

hypotheses.what_would_change_this: A climbing heap or CPU trend in the minutes leading up to each restart would support this instead of a deterministic offset failure.

ruled_out.reason: Different service (nightly-settlement-batch), no shared correlation ID, resolved on its own well before the real incident window.
Same unrelated nightly-settlement-batch job, coincidentally timed inside the incident window but with no correlation to order-orchestrator.

checks.action: Query the committed consumer offset for order-enriched-cg on order.enriched
checks.if_result_a: Offset static at 4481209 across repeated queries — supports hypothesis 1 (poison message)
checks.if_result_b: Offset advancing, even slowly — supports hypothesis 2 (resource pressure) instead

checks.action: Pull heap and CPU metrics for order-orchestrator across the last 4 restarts
checks.if_result_a: Heap/CPU flat at baseline through every restart — rules out hypothesis 2
checks.if_result_b: Heap or CPU climbing before each restart — supports hypothesis 2

checks.action: Fetch and manually deserialise the record at offset 4481209
checks.if_result_a: Record contains the malformed negative-quantity line from PB-4471 — confirms the exact payload and enables a targeted skip/patch
checks.if_result_b: Record deserialises cleanly — reopens the investigation entirely

recovery.proposal: Manually skip the poisoned record at order.enriched offset 4,481,209 (commit the consumer past it without processing), route a copy of the raw record to a newly-configured DLQ for later reprocessing, then resume the order-enriched-cg consumer group.
recovery.risk: The order carried by the skipped record (from partner batch PB-4471) will not be enriched automatically and needs manual reconciliation; if other malformed lines exist later in the same batch, the consumer could poison again on the next one.
recovery.rollback: If the skip causes unexpected downstream errors, pause the consumer group again and restore from the last known-good offset checkpoint (4,481,209) before the skip was committed.

diagnosis.post_incident_note: INC0098462 — root cause: malformed line in partner B2B batch PB-4471 (negative lineQty on SKU MRD-88213) caused a deserialisation exception that crash-looped order-orchestrator on a fixed 3-minute restart interval, with the order.enriched consumer offset frozen at 4,481,209 from 11:16 onward. Mitigated via manual offset skip + new DLQ routing once approved. Follow-up: add schema validation at the partner feed ingestion boundary so malformed lines are rejected before reaching order.enriched, and configure a DLQ policy on this topic so future poison messages don't require a manual skip.
